title: Report provenance record
description: The report.json written beside every published page. This is the source of truth for the report: the page is a rendering of it. Site-level figures are built from these records and never scraped from rendered HTML, which is what stops a claim that exists only in prose becoming a site-level number. Where the page and this record disagree, this record is what the run produced. A retired report keeps a stub page naming its successor and has no report.json, so it drops out of every index and total with no special case.

report_id.description: Becomes a public URL path and is permanent. Changing it breaks every link already sent. Certain names are reserved for generated source hub pages; publishing a report under one must be refused, because staging a report removes its destination directory first.

license.description: COMPUTED, never chosen. A report takes the most restrictive terms any contributing feed imposes, read from derivatives_license in the feed registry. Two different share-alike licences are refused rather than ranked, because that combination cannot be satisfied at all.

floors.description: Measured false-positive floors that licensed the claims on this page. A label with no measured floor at that site gets no card, however confident the model was.

runs.description: Run identifiers that produced this report.

review_status.description: Required, and must be a status this schema recognises. A report that will not say what it is cannot be checked, so an absent or unknown status is refused rather than waved through. 'model candidate' means a queue: model output published before anyone judged it. Nothing on such a page is an identification, and floors do not license it; an unreviewed automated run is a model candidate. 'source quality gap' publishes an absence of usable source and is the only status excused from the detection checks described under counts.

series.description: Position in a recurring series, where the report belongs to one.

review.description: Human review metadata, where a person has judged this page.

coverage_gaps.description: Known periods with no usable signal, stated rather than left to be inferred from a low count.

media_quality.description: How the bundled media was selected and what it is. Lets a reader tell a full source window from a trimmed clip.

model_refresh.description: Whether the model output behind this page is current or was inherited from an earlier run.

quality.description: The selection rule in force and the public claim it supports. Stating both is what lets a reader check that the claim does not exceed the rule.

redaction_allowances.description: Every redaction override used, recorded in the published artifact rather than only in somebody's shell history. An override takes a specific literal string, never a rule.

label.description: May contain a comma. Join several labels with a separator that cannot occur inside one, or three sites read as four.

model.description: model_name is canonical: resolve it through one model registry, with aliases for earlier spellings, so one detector does not reach manifests under several names. Fill license, lineage and caveat from that registry at publish rather than leaving them null: a published claim whose licence is unrecorded cannot be cleared. model_version is a property of the run, not the model.

code_commit.description: The full commit that built the report, read from version control. Null when that cannot be answered, never an abbreviation or a guess. A published claim with no recorded commit cannot be reproduced.

floor.description: A false-positive rate measured for one label at one site. Floors are per site: pooling them lets a busy site clear a threshold on its own volume and then license claims at a quiet site that never earned one.

window.description: All three fields are nullable, and null carries meaning. What is required depends on the unit of analysis. Audio windows have a fixed duration, so a report that analysed windows must state start, end and usable_hours, all derived from the run. Stills have no duration: never state hours for them. Video hours come only from the clip durations the run recorded; a run that recorded none yields dates and no hours. A null window on a report that lists runs is a warning, not a refusal, because detections are never held back over a provenance field; the site shows that report's dates as inferred. What is NOT acceptable is a report that states no coverage anywhere: a day with no detections and a day with no recording look identical on a count, and coverage is the only thing that separates them.

start_utc.description: A date (YYYY-MM-DD) or a UTC date-time.

end_utc.description: A date (YYYY-MM-DD) or a UTC date-time. An end stamped at exactly midnight is an exclusive bound.

usable_hours.description: Hours of USABLE signal, which is a stricter test than hours recording. A sum over nodes, not a duration. READ from run artifacts, never typed: a hand-entered figure is a claim about provenance rather than provenance. Null where coverage is counted another way; see the note on this object.

counts.description: Deliberately open. The bundling counts are common to every report; the rest are specific to what a given run measured, and inventing a fixed vocabulary for them would mean either lying or padding with zeros. Name each count for what it holds (model_candidates, marine_review_candidates, source_units_with_positive_segment), so a reader knows whether a number counts boxes, rows or windows before opening its definition. A null is an absence and a zero is a claim: never write a zero where the run could not measure. When review_status asserts detections, the publishing gate also requires three things this schema cannot express, because the key of a positive count varies by kind: at least one count whose key names a detection, positive or candidate; a positive_definition; and media on the page or an evidence_waiver.

assets_missing.description: Must be 0 in a published report. Every local reference has to resolve inside the bundle, or publish refuses.

assets_dropped_for_budget.description: What did not fit the byte budget. Counted and reported on the page, never dropped silently.

source_paths_unparsable.description: Source paths that failed the lake path contract. Counted and reported rather than silently averaged in.

windows_analysed.description: Audio windows analysed. On a duration-bearing site, a non-zero value requires window.usable_hours and window dates.

frames_analysed.description: Stills analysed. Never converted to hours.

source_segments.description: Video clips read, including clips with no detections: coverage is what was watched, not what was found.

days_covered.description: Distinct calendar days the data carries, read from the data rather than from two window endpoints.

windows_by_camera.description: Per-camera coverage, keyed by the feed registry's camera id. Every key must be declared in sites: a camera that contributed data and is not credited is an attribution failure, and sites is what the rights gate reads.

positive_definition.description: What the positive counts count, in words a reader can check against the run. Required whenever a positive count is reported. 'Window with a positive model verdict' and 'window with at least one positive segment' differed by 40% at one station.

positive_definition_provenance.description: Where a definition backfilled after publication came from. Absent when the run wrote the definition itself. not_recoverable records that the question cannot be answered, and such a report gains no numbers.

evidence_waiver.description: Why a report with positive counts shows no media. The only way to publish detections a reader cannot see or hear, and the reason lands in the published artifact.

contaminant_screening.description: What was done about each known contaminant at the declared sites (a site-specific sound or object the model fires on), naming each one. Disclosure is required, not a particular choice: 'not screened, counts include it' passes; silence does not.

rightsRecord.description: Copied from the feed registry at publish time, so the report carries the rights position that was in force when it was built.

finding.description: One highlighted result. Two generations exist: earlier findings carry a prose 'evidence' field, later ones carry structured 'id', 'model', 'confidence' and 'timestamp'. Both are valid; new work should emit the structured form.

taxonomy.description: One label, or several where a finding sits under more than one.

confidence.description: The model score, a number in 0..1, and the publishing gate refuses anything else. A string is accepted here only so archived records still validate: published data once held prose ('Ecotype 1.00 Southern Resident, OrcaHello 0.97'), which a consumer cannot compare, sort or threshold, and which records the numbers it describes nowhere machine-readable. Emit a number and put the sentence in 'summary'.

at_utc.description: The instant a moment was observed. Omit it for a statement about a dataset, such as a rate over a month; a card then shows the window it was drawn from, never an invented instant.

path.description: Relative, content-addressed, and resolving inside the bundle. An image referenced from forty cards is copied once.
